name: support_tickets
description: Support tickets filed by customers of "Taskline", a fictional B2B project-management SaaS.
context:
Taskline has Free, Team and Enterprise plans. Enterprise customers have SSO, audit logs and a
4-hour first-response SLA; Team has 24h; Free is best-effort. Common issues: SSO/SAML setup,
Jira/GitHub/Slack integrations, permission confusion, billing (seat counts, invoices, VAT),
data import from Asana/Trello, API rate limits, slow boards with >5k tasks, mobile sync bugs.
Agents tag tickets and set priority; urgent is reserved for outages or data loss.

properties.name: contact_email
properties.description: Contact's work email on the company's (fictional) domain.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: Ticket subject line as written by the customer.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The customer's initial message, with the concrete details an agent would need.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Short lowercase agent tags in kebab-case.

fields.name: resolution_hours
fields.description: Hours from creation to resolution; null unless status is resolved or closed.

fields.name: csat
fields.description: Customer satisfaction score; only for resolved/closed tickets, and not always given.

rules: Free-plan customers have 1-10 seats, Team 5-300, Enterprise 200+. SSO issues only occur on Enterprise.
resolution_hours and csat are null when status is open or pending_customer.
Urgent tickets describe an outage, data loss or a blocked team, and their body reads as urgent.
Tags must be consistent with the category and body.
checks: status in ('resolved', 'closed') or (resolution_hours is None and csat is None)
